quotes.text: Mail authentication proves that a server was authorized to send a message, and it proves how that message was handled during transport. But it does not prove that the sender has actual authority.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws the key line between mail authentication and business authority.

quotes.text: Identity tells you who the person is, but authority tells you what that person is allowed to do. Those are not the same thing.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Core distinction behind authority-based credential design.

quotes.text: The message can start the process, but it is physically unable to finish it. Authority moves out of the inbox and into the control point where the business decision is actually enforced.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the new defense pattern against deepfake BEC.

quotes.text: Do not issue credentials that merely confirm someone is employed. Issue credentials that map directly to authority in the real business process.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear design rule for verifiable credentials.

quotes.text: If the business system cannot ask for proof and stop the action when that proof is missing, the control stays optional. And we know that optional controls never survive real-world pressure.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why verification must live inside the business workflow.

takeaways: SPF, DKIM and DMARC prove how an email was sent and handled, but they cannot prove that the sender has authority for the requested action.
Microsoft Entra Verified ID lets workflows require a signed, verifiable credential that proves specific authority at the moment of a high-risk action.
Design narrow, quickly revocable credentials around decision rights and start with one high-risk workflow such as treasury approvals or executive help desk resets.
hook: AI-written emails and cloned voices make fraudulent payment requests look perfectly legitimate, and classic email authentication cannot stop them. This episode is for security architects, identity teams and finance leaders who need a stronger defense against deepfake business email compromise. Learn how Microsoft Entra Verified ID moves trust from the message to provable authority at the point of decision.
